facts.summary: Florida has no state overtime statute; overtime is governed entirely by the federal FLSA (time-and-a-half after 40 hours per week, no daily overtime).
facts.citation: No Florida overtime statute; see Fla. Stat. ch. 448
facts.notes: Florida statutes contain no overtime provision; the state defers to federal FLSA. The floridajobs.org page was reachable via search but returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch; verify the URL in a browser. Source-domain exception: Florida's Dept of Commerce (the state's labor/wage agency) operates on floridajobs.org, not a .gov domain -- no floridajobs.gov or equivalent .gov site exists for this agency (confirmed no DNS resolution); floridajobs.org is treated as the official agency site for this dataset.

facts.summary: Florida's minimum wage is $14.00/hour (effective Sept 30, 2025), scheduled to rise to $15.00/hour on Sept 30, 2026; tipped minimum is $10.98 (tip credit $3.02), rising to $11.98.
facts.citation: Fla. Const. art. X, s. 24; Fla. Stat. 448.110
facts.notes: Higher than federal $7.25. As of this re-check (2026-08-08) the current rate is still $14.00; it increases to $15.00 on 2026-09-30 (the final scheduled step of the 2020 constitutional amendment, Fla. Const. art. X, s. 24) and this fact must be updated to value 15.00 / tipped 11.98 on or after that date -- VERIFY AND UPDATE 2026-09-30. Beginning 2027 the Dept of Commerce adjusts the rate annually for inflation, so this figure should also be re-checked each year thereafter.

facts.summary: The Florida Civil Rights Act adds 'marital status' beyond the federal set; it also expressly protects pregnancy, handicap/disability, and (via handicap) AIDS/HIV status.
facts.notes: Full FCRA list: race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, handicap, marital status. The genuine ADD versus federal Title VII/ADA/ADEA is 'marital status'. Florida law does not statewide list sexual orientation or gender identity.

facts.summary: The Florida Civil Rights Act covers employers with 15 or more employees for each working day in 20+ calendar weeks, the same threshold as federal Title VII.
facts.notes: Same 15-employee threshold as federal; not lower. Recorded because coverage is a listed topic.

facts.summary: A discrimination complaint must be filed with the Florida Commission on Human Relations within 365 days of the alleged violation, longer than the federal 180/300-day EEOC deadlines.
facts.notes: FCHR is Florida's FEPA. Separate downstream deadlines apply to filing the civil lawsuit after an FCHR/EEOC determination (amended effective July 1, 2026); this fact covers only the administrative charge deadline. Source-domain exception: the Florida Commission on Human Relations (see agencies.discrimination) operates on fchr.myflorida.com, not a .gov domain -- no fchr.gov or equivalent .gov site exists (confirmed no DNS resolution); myflorida.com is the state's official web platform and fchr.myflorida.com is treated as the official agency site for this dataset.

facts.value: Florida Private Sector Whistleblower's Act, Fla. Stat. 448.101-448.105
facts.summary: Florida's Private Whistleblower's Act protects private employees (employers with 10+ employees) from retaliation for disclosing, or refusing to participate in, a violation of law, rule, or regulation.
facts.notes: Statute number 448.102 confirmed via official statute site listing; exact section text not individually fetched. 'Employer' 10+ employees per 448.101(3). Remedies include reinstatement, back pay, and attorney's fees under 448.103.

facts.value: 2 years (general wages); 4 years, or 5 years if willful, for minimum-wage claims
facts.summary: General actions to recover wages/overtime have a 2-year limitations period, while minimum-wage claims carry a 4-year period (5 years for willful violations) under the state constitution.
facts.citation: Fla. Stat. 95.11(5)(d); Fla. Const. art. X, s. 24(e); Fla. Stat. 448.110(8)
facts.notes: 95.11(5)(d) sets a 2-year SOL for general wage/overtime recovery. Minimum-wage claims follow the constitutional 4-year (5-year willful) period mirroring the federal FLSA; 448.110(8) ties the period to 95.11. Confirm which period applies to the specific claim type.
